chapters: And king Dovid was old, he came into his old age, and they covered him with clothes, but he was not warmed.

And his servants said to him, "Let them seek for my master the king a young girl, a virgin, and she shall stand before the king, and she shall be to him a warmer, and she shall lie in your lap, and it shall be warm for my master the king."
And they sought a beautiful young girl throughout the borders of Yisroel, and found Avishag the Shunamit and brought her to the king.
And the young girl was very beautiful, and she was a warmer to the king, and she ministered to him, but the king did not know her.
And Adoniyah the son of Chaggit exalted himself saying: 'I will be king,' and he made for himself chariots and horsemen and fifty men to run before him.
And his father had not angered him all his days saying, "Why have you done so?" And he too was of very handsome appearance, and she bore him after Avshalom.
And he conferred with Yoav the son of Tzeruyah and with Evyatar the priest and they helped after Adoniyah.
And Tzadok the priest and Benayahu the son of Yehoyada, and Natan the prophet, and Shimi and Rei, and the mighty men, who were with Dovid, were not with Adoniyah.
And Adoniyah slew sheep and oxen and fatlings, by the stone of Zochelet which is beside Ein-Rogel, and he called all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Yehudah, the kings servants.
And Natan the prophet and Benayahu and the mighty men and his brother, Shlomo, he did not call.
And Natan said to Bat-Sheva, Shlomo's mother, saying, "You have surely heard that Adoniyah the son of Chaggit has reigned, and our master, Dovid, did not know.
And now come and I shall council you with advice, and you shall save your life and the life of your son Shlomo.

Go and come to king Dovid, and you shall say to him, 'Surely, you, my master the king, did swear to your maid saying that, 'Shlomo your son will reign after me and he shall sit upon my throne,' Now why did Adoniyah reign?"
Behold, you are talking there with the king, and I shall come in after you and I shall complete your words."
And Bat Sheva came in unto the king, into the chamber; and the king was very old; and Avishag the Shunamit ministered the king.
And Bat-Sheva bowed her head, and prostrated herself unto the king, and the king said, "What is your?"
And she said to him, "My master, you swore by Havayah your Elokim to your maid, that, 'Shlomo, your son, shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne.'
And now, behold Adoniyah has reigned, and now my master the king, you did not know.
And he has slain oxen and fatlings and sheep in abundance and he called all the king's sons and Evyatar the priest and Yoav the general of the army, but Shlomo, your servant, he did not call.
And you, my master the king, the eyes of all Yisroel are upon you, that you should tell them, who shall sit on the throne of my master the king after him.
And when my master the king shall sleep with his fathers, and I and my son Shlomo shall be offenders."
And behold, she was still speaking with the king, and Natan the prophet came.
And they told the king saying, "Behold, Natan the prophet." And he came in before the king and he prostrated himself unto the king upon his face, to the ground.
And Natan said, "My master the king, did you say 'Adoniyah shall reign after me and he shall sit upon my throne?'"

For he has gone down this day and has slain oxen and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and he called all the King's sons, and the officers of the army, and Evyatar the priest, and behold they eat and drink before him, and they said, "Long live King Adoniyah."
And me, me your servant, and Tzadok the priest and Benayahu the son of Yehoiada and Shlomo, your servant, he did not call.
If this matter stems from my master the king, you have not informed your servant who should sit on the throne of my master the king after him.
And king Dovid answered and said, "Call Bat Sheva to me. And she came before the king and stood before the king.
And he swore and said, " Elokim lives who redeemed my soul from all distress.
Indeed, as I swore to you by Havayah Elokim of Yisroel saying, 'Surely Shlomo, your son, shall reign after me and he shall sit on my throne in my stead,' surely, so will I do this day."
And Bat-Sheva bowed face to the earth, and she prostrated herself to the king and said, "Let my master King Dovid live forever."
And king Dovid said, "Call Tzadok the priest to me, and Natan the prophet, and Benayahu the son of Yehoyada," and they came before the king.
And the king said to them, "Take with you the servants of your master, and you shall cause Shlomo my son to ride on my own mule, and bring him down to Gichon.
And Tzadok the priest and Natan the prophet shall anoint him there as king over Yisroel, and blow the horn and say, " live King Shlomo."
And you shall come up after him, and he shall come and sit on my throne, and he shall reign in my stead, and I have appointed him to be ruler over Yisroel and over Yehudah.
And Benayahu the son of Yehoyada answered the king and said, "Amen, Havayah, Elokim of my master the king say so.
As Havayah was with my master the king, so shall He be with Shlomo and make his throne greater than the throne of my master King Dovid.
And Tzadok the priest and Natan the prophet and Benayahu the son of Yehoyada and the archers and the slingers went down, and caused Shlomo to ride on king Dovid's mule and brought him to Gichon.
And Tzadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tabernacle and anointed Shlomo, and they blew the horn, and all the people said, "Long live king Shlomo."
And all the people came up after him, and the people played the flutes and rejoiced with great joy, and the earth was rent by their sound.
And Adoniyah and all the guests who with him heard and they had finished eating, and Yoav heard the sound of the horn, he said, "Why the noise of the city turbulent?"
he was still speaking, and behold Yehonatan the son of Evyatar the priest came, and Adoniyah said, "Come in, for you are a valiant man, and bring good tidings."
And Yehonatan answered and said to Adoniyah, "But our master king Dovid has made Shlomo king.
And the king sent with him Tzadok the priest and Natan the prophet and Benayahu the son of Yehoyada and the archers and the slingers, and they have caused him to ride on the king's mule.
And Tzadok the priest and Natan the prophet have anointed him king in Gichon, and they have come up from their rejoicing, and the city was turbulent, this is the noise you have heard.
And also Shlomo was sitting on the throne of the kingdom.

And also the king's servants came to bless our master king Dovid saying, ' Elokim make the name of Shlomo better than your name, and make his throne greater than your throne,' and the king bowed down upon the bed.
And also this the king said, 'Blessed be Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel, who has given this the one day to sit on my throne, and my eyes seeing.'"
And all Adoniyah's guests trembled and arose and went each man to his way.
And Adoniyah was fearful of Shlomo, and he rose and went, and he took hold of the horns of the altar.

And it was told to Shlomo saying, behold Adoniyah fears king Shlomo, and behold he has taken hold of the horns of the altar saying, "Let king Shlomo swear to me today, that he shall not kill his servant with the sword."
And Shlomo said, "If he will be a valiant man, even one hair of his shall not fall to the ground, but if wickedness will be found in him, he shall die.
And King Shlomo sent, and they brought him down from the altar, and he came in and prostrated himself before king Shlomo, and Shlomo said to him. "Go to your house."
And the days of Dovid drew near that he should die; and he charged Shlomo, his son, saying:
"I go the way of all the earth; you shall be strong, therefore, and show yourself a man;

And keep the charge of Havayah your Elokim to walk in His ways, to keep His statutes, and His commandments, and His judgments, and His testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moshe, that you may prosper in all that you do, and wherever you turn;

That Havayah may continue His word which He spoke concerning me, saying, 'If your children take heed to their way, to walk before Me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not fail you,' He said, 'a man on the throne of Yisroel.'

Moreover, you also know what Yoav the son of Tzeruyah did to me, what he did to the two captains of the hosts of Yisroel, to Avner the son of Ner, and to Amasa the son of Yeter, whom he slew, and shed the blood of war in peace and put the blood of war upon his girdle about his loins, and in his shoes that on his feet.
And you shall do according to your wisdom, and do not let his hoary head go down to the grave in peace.
But show kindness to the children of Barzilai the Giladi, and let them be of those that eat at your table, for so did they befriend me when I fled from Avshalom your brother.

And, behold, there is with you Shimi the son of Gera the Binyamini of Bachurim, who cursed me with a grievous curse on the day when I went to Machanayim, and he came down to meet me at the Yarden, and I swore to him by Havayah, saying, 'I will not put you to death with the sword.'
And now hold him not guiltless, for you are a wise man, and you will surely know what you ought to do to him, and you shall bring his hoary head down to the grave with blood."
And Dovid slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of Dovid.
And the days that Dovid reigned over Yisroel forty years, seven years he reigned in Chevron, and in Yerushalayim he reigned thirty-three years.
And Shlomo sat upon the throne of Dovid his father, and his kingdom was firmly established.
And Adoniyah the son of Chaggit came to Bat Sheva, the mother of Shlomo, and she said, "Do you come peaceably?" And he said, "Peaceably."
And he said, "I have something to say to you." And she said, "Say on."
And he said, "You know that the kingdom was mine, and all Yisroel set their faces on me, that I should reign, but the kingdom turned about, and has become my brother's, for it was his from Havayah.
And now I ask one petition of you, do not refuse me, and she said to him, "Say on."
And he said, "Say, I beg of you, to Shlomo the king, for he will not refuse you, that he give me Avishag the Shunamit as a wife.
And she said, "Good, I will speak for you to the king."

And Bat Sheva came into king Shlomo to speak to him for Adoniyah. And the king rose up to meet her and bowed himself to her, and sat down on his throne, and caused a seat to be set for the king's mother, and she sat at his right hand.
And she said, "I ask one small petition of you, do not refuse me," and the king said to her, "Ask on, my mother, for I will not refuse you."
And she said, "Let Avishag the Shunamit be given to Adoniyah, your brother, as a wife."

And king Shlomo answered and said to his mother, "And why do you ask Avishag the Shunamit for Adoniyah? Ask for him the kingdom, for he is my elder brother, and to him, and Evyatar the priest, and Yoav the son of Tzeruyah."
And king Shlomo swore by Havayah, saying, "Elokim do so to me, and more also, if Adoniyah has spoken this word with his life."
And now, Havayah lives, Who has established me, and set me on the throne of Dovid, my father, and Who has made me a house, as He had promised, that Adoniyah shall be put to death this day.
And king Shlomo sent by the hand of Benayahu the son of Yehoyada, and he fell upon him that he died.

And to Evyatar the priest the king said, "Go to Anatot to your own fields, for you deservant of death, but on this day I will not put you to death, because you did bear the ark of Havayah Elokim before Dovid, my father, and because you were afflicted in all wherein my father was afflicted.
And Shlomo banished Evyatar from being priest to Havayah, that he might fulfill the word of Havayah, which He spoke concerning the house of Eli in Shilo.
And the tidings came to Yoav, for Yoav had turned after Adoniyah, and after Avshalom he did not turn, and Yoav fled into the tabernacle of Havayah and took hold of the horns of the altar.
And it was told king Shlomo, that Yoav fled into the tabernacle of Havayah and behold by the altar, and Shlomo sent Benayahu the son of Yehoyada, saying, "Go, fall upon him."

And Benayahu came to the tabernacle of Havayah, and said to him, "Thus said the king, 'Come forth.'" And he said, "No, for I will die here." And Benayahu brought back word to the king, saying, "Thus spoke Yoav, and thus he answered me."
And the king said to him, "Do as he said, and fall upon him, and bury him, that you may take away the innocent blood, which Yoav shed, from me, and from my father's house."

And Havayah shall return his blood upon his own head, that he fell upon two men more righteous and better than he, and slew them with the sword, and my father Dovid did not know, Avner the son of Ner, captain of the host of Yisroel, and Amasa the son of Yeter, captain of the host of Yehudah.

And their blood shall return upon the head of Yoav, and upon the head of his seed forever, but upon Dovid, and upon his seed, and upon his house, and upon his throne, there shall be peace forever from Havayah.
And Benayahu the son of Yehoyada went up, and fell upon him, and slew him, and he was buried in his own house in the wilderness.
And the king put Benayahu the son of Yehoyada in his place over the host, and Tzadok the priest did the king put in the place of Evyatar.
And the king sent and called for Shimi, and said to him, "Build for yourself a house in Yerushalayim, and dwell there, and do not go forth here or there."
And it shall be, on the day you go out, and you pass over the Kidron Valley you shall know for certain that you shall surely die; your blood shall be upon your own head.
And Shimi said to the king, "The saying is good; as my master the king has said, so will your servant do; and Shimi dwelt in Yerushalayim many days.
And it came to pass at the end of three years, that two of Shimi's slaves ran away to Achish the son of Ma'achah, king of Gat, and they told Shimi, saying, "Behold your slaves are in Gat.
And Shimi arose, saddled his ass, and went to Gat to Achish, to seek his slaves, and Shimi went, and brought his slaves from Gat.
And it was told to Shlomo, that Shimi had gone from Yerushalayim to Gat and had returned.

And the king sent and called for Shimi, and said to him, "Did I not make you swear by Havayah, and forewarned you, saying, "On the day that you go out and go here or there, know for certain, that you shall surely die, and you said to me, "The word is good I have accepted."
And why have you not kept the oath of Havayah, and the commandment with which I have charged you?"
And the king said to Shimi, "You know all the wickedness, which your heart knew secretly, that you did to Dovid, my father; and Havayah shall return your wickedness upon your own head."
And king Shlomo blessed, and the throne of Dovid shall be established before Havayah forever.
And the king commanded Benayahu the son of Yehoyada, and he went out and fell upon him, and he died; and the kingdom was established in the hand of Shlomo.

And Shlomo became allied by marriage to Paroh king of Mitzrayim, and took Paroh's daughter, and brought her into the city of Dovid, until he had completed building his own house, and the house of Havayah, and the wall of Yerushalayim round about.
Only the people sacrificed in the high places, because there was no house built unto the name of Havayah, until those days.
And Shlomo loved Havayah, walking in the statutes of Dovid his father; only he sacrificed and burnt incense in the high places.
And the king went to Givon to sacrifice there; for that the great high place; a thousand burnt offerings did Shlomo offer upon that altar.
In Givon Havayah appeared to Shlomo in a dream by night; and Elokim said, "Ask what I shall give you."

And Shlomo said, "You have done Your servant Dovid my father great kindness, as he walked before you in truth, and in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart with You; and You have kept for him this great kindness, that You have given him a son to sit on his throne, as this day.
And now, O Havayah my Elokim, You have made Your servant king instead of Dovid my father; and I a little child; I do not know to go out or come in.
And your servant in the midst of Your people which you have chosen, a great people, that cannot be numbered nor counted for multitude.
Give Your servant an understanding heart to judge Your people, that I may discern between good and bad; for who is able to judge this Your great people?"
And the speech pleased Havayah, that Shlomo had asked this thing.

And Elokim said to him, "Because you have asked this thing, and have not asked for yourself long life; neither have you asked riches for yourself, nor have you asked the life of your enemies; but have asked for yourself understanding to discern judgment.
Behold, I have done according to your word; behold, I have given you a wise and understanding heart; so that there was none like you before you, nor after you shall any arise like you.
And I have also given you that which you have not asked, both riches and honor, so that there shall not be any among the kings like you all your days.
And if you walk in My ways, to keep My statutes and My commandments, as your father Dovid did walk, then I will lengthen your days."

And Shlomo awoke, and behold a dream. And he came to Yerushalayim, and stood before the ark of the covenant of Havayah, and offered up burnt offerings, and offered peace offerings, and made a feast for all his servants.
Then came two women, harlots, to the king, and stood before him.
And the one woman said, "Oh, my master, I and this woman dwell in one house; and I gave birth to a child with her in the house.
And it came to pass the third day after I had given birth, that this woman gave birth also; and we together, no stranger with us in the house, besides us two in the house.
And this woman's son died at night; because she had lain on him.
And she arose in the middle of the night and took my son from beside me, while your handmaid slept, and laid him in her bosom, and laid her dead son in my bosom.
And I rose in the morning to nurse my son, and behold he was dead, but I looked closely at him in the morning, and behold, it was not my son whom I had borne."
And the other woman said, "Not so, the living my son, and the dead your son," and this one said, "Not so, the dead your son, and the living my son." Thus they spoke before the king.
And the king said, "This one says, 'This my son that lives, and your son the dead, and the other says, 'Not so, your son the dead, and my son the living.' "
And the king said, "Fetch me a sword." And they brought a sword before the king.
And the king said, "Divide the living child in two, and give half to the one, and half to the other.

And the woman whose son the live one, said to the king, for her compassion was aroused for her son, and she said, "O my master, give her the living child, and by no means slay him." But the other said, "Let it be neither mine nor yours, divide."
And the king answered and said, "Give her the living child, and by no means slay him: she his mother."
And all Yisroel heard of the judgment which the king had judged; and they feared the king; for they saw that the wisdom of Elokim in him to do judgment.
And King Shlomo was king over all Yisroel.
And these the princes whom he had, Azaryahu the son of Tzadok the priest.
Elichoref and Ahiah, the sons of Shisha, scribes, Yehoshafat the son of Achilud the recorder.
And Benayahu the son of Yehoyada over the host, and Tzadok and Evyatar the priests.
And Azaryahu the son of Natan over the officers, and Zavud the son of Natan principal officer, and the king's friend.
And Achishar over the household, and Adoniram the son of Avda over the levy.
And Shlomo had twelve officers over all Yisroel, who provided victuals for the king and his household, each man had to make provision for a month in the year.
And these are their names, the son of Hur, on Mount Efraim.
The son of Deker, in Makaz, and in Sha'alvim, and Beit-Shemesh, and Elon-beth-hanan.
The son of Chesed, in Aruvot, to him Sochoh, and all the land of Chefer.
The son of Avinadav, all the region of Dor; Tafat the daughter of Shlomo was to him as a wife.
Ba'anah the son of Achilud, Ta'anach and Megiddo, and all Beit-She'an which is beside Tzareitanah beneath Yizre'el, from Beit-She'an to Avel-mechola, as far as beyond Yokme'am.
The son of Gever, in Ramot-gilead, to him the towns of Yair the son of Menasheh, which are in Gilad; to him the region of Argob which is in Bashan, sixty great cities with walls and brazen bars.
Achindav the son of Ido, to Machanayim.
Achima'atz in Naftali, also he took Basmat the daughter of Shlomo as a wife.
Ba'anah the son of Chushai in Asher and in Alot.
Yehoshafat the son of Paruach in Yissachar.
Shimi the son of Elah, in Binyamin.
Gever the son of Uri in the country of Gilad, the land of Sichon king of the Emorim, and of Og king of Bashan, and one officer that was in the land.
Yehudah and Yisroel many, as the sand which by the sea in multitude, eating and drinking, and rejoicing.
And Shlomo reigned over all the kingdoms from the River to the land of the Pelishtim, and to the border of Mitzrayim, they brought presents, and served Shlomo all the days of his life.
And Shlomo's provision for one day was thirty measures of fine flour, and sixty measures of meal.
Ten fat oxen, and twenty oxen out of the pastures, and a hundred sheep, besides harts, and deer, and fallow deer, and fatted fowl.
For he had dominion over all on this side of the river, from Tifsach even to Azah, over all the kings on this side of the river, and he had peace on all sides around.
And Yehudah and Yisroel dwelt safely, every man under his vine and under his fig-tree, from Dan even to Be'er Sheva, all the days of Shlomo.
And Shlomo had forty thousand stalls of horses for his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen.
And these officers provided victuals for king Shlomo, and for all that came unto king Shlomo's table, every man his month, they lacked nothing.
And the barley and the straw for the horses and swift steeds they brought to the place where he would be there, every man according to his charge.
And Elokim gave Shlomo wisdom and understanding exceedingly much, and largeness of heart, as the sand that on the seashore.
And Shlomo's wisdom was greater than the wisdom of all the children of the east, and all the wisdom of Mitzrayim.
And he was wiser than all men, than Eitan the Ezrachi, and Heiman, and Kalkol, and Darda, the sons of Machol, and his fame was in all the nations round about.
And he spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs were a thousand and five.
And he spoke of trees, from the cedar tree that in Levanon and to the hyssop that springs out of the wall, and he spoke of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of the creeping things, and of the fishes.
And they came of all peoples to hear the wisdom of Shlomo, from all kings of the earth, who had heard his wisdom.
And Chiram king of Tzor sent his servants to Shlomo, for he had heard that they had anointed him king in place of his father, for Chiram was ever a lover of Dovid.
And Shlomo sent to Chiram, saying.
You knew my father, Dovid, that he could not build a house for the name of Havayah his Elokim, because of the wars which surrounded him, until Havayah put them under the soles of his feet.
And now Havayah my Elokim has given me rest on every side, neither adversary nor evil occurrence.

And, behold, I purpose to build a house for the name of Havayah my Elokim, as Havayah spoke to Dovid my father, saying, 'Your son whom I will set upon your throne in your place, he shall build a house for My name.'

And now, command that they hew me cedar trees out of Levanon, and my servants shall be with your servants, and I will give you hire for your servants according to all that you shall say, for you know that not among us any who is skilled to hew timber like the Tzidonim.
And it was, when Chiram heard the words of Shlomo, that he rejoiced greatly, and said, "Blessed be Havayah this day, who has given to Dovid a wise son over this great people."
And Chiram sent to Shlomo, saying, "I have heard that which you have sent me, I will do all your desires concerning cedar wood, and concerning cypress wood.

My servants shall bring down from Levanon to the sea, and I will make them into rafts by the sea to the place that you shall send me, and will separate them there, and you will transport, and you shall accomplish my desire, in giving food for my household.
And Chiram gave Shlomo cedar wood and cypress wood all his desire.
And Shlomo gave Chiram twenty thousand measures of wheat food to his household, and twenty measures of beaten oil, thus gave Shlomo to Chiram year by year.
And Havayah gave Shlomo wisdom, as He had promised him, and there was peace between Chiram and Shlomo, and they both made a league together.
And King Shlomo raised a levy out of all Yisroel, and the levy was thirty thousand men.
And he sent them to Levanon, ten thousand a month alternately, a month they were in Levanon, two months at home, and Adoniram over the levy.
And Shlomo had seventy thousand who bore burdens, and eighty thousand hewers in the mountains.
Besides Shlomo's chief officers that were over the work, three thousand and three hundred, who bore rule over the people that wrought in the work.
And the king commanded, and they quarried great stones, heavy stones, to lay the foundation of the house hewn stone.
And Shlomo's builders and Chiram's builders and the Gevalim did hew, and they prepared the timber and the stones to build the house.

And it was in the four hundred and eightieth year after the departure of the children of Yisroel from Mitzrayim, in the fourth year, in the month Ziv, which the second month of Shlomo's reign over Yisroel, that he did build the house of Havayah.
And the house which king Shlomo built for Havayah, the length thereof sixty cubits, and the breadth thereof twenty cubits, and the height thereof thirty cubits.
And the porch before the temple of the house, twenty cubits the length thereof, before the breadth of the house, ten cubits the breadth thereof before the house.
And he made for the house windows broad without, and narrow within.
And against the wall of the house he built a chamber round about, the walls of the house round about, of the temple and of the sanctuary, and he made chambers round about.

The nethermost chamber five cubits broad, and the middle six cubits broad, and the third seven cubits broad, for he made rebatements in the house round about on the outside, that should not have hold in the walls of the house.
And the house, when it was in building, was built of stone finished at the quarry, and there was neither hammer nor axe any tool of iron heard in the house, while it was in building.
The door of the lowest chamber in the right side of the house, and with winding stairs they went up into the middle, and from the middle into the third.
And he built the house, and finished it, and he covered the house with panelling and joined planks of cedar.
And he built the chambers against all the house, five cubits high; and he covered the house with timber of cedar.
And the word of Havayah came to Shlomo saying,

this house which you are building, if you walk in My statutes, and execute My ordinances, and keep all My commandments to walk in them; then will I establish My word with you, which I spoke to Dovid your father.
And I will dwell among the children of Yisroel, and will not forsake My people, Yisroel.
And Shlomo built the house and finished it.

And he built the walls of the house within boards of cedar; from the floor of the house till the joists of the ceiling, he covered them on the inside with wood; and he covered the floor of the house with boards of cypress.
And he built the twenty cubits at the end of the house with boards of cedar; from the floor unto the joists, and he built it within, for a Sanctuary, for the Holy of Holies.
And forty cubits was the house, that is the Temple before.
And the cedar of the house within carved with knobs and open flowers; all cedar; there was no stone seen.
And the Sanctuary he prepared in the midst of the house within, to set there the ark of the covenant of Havayah.
And within the Sanctuary twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in breadth, and twenty cubits its height, and he overlaid it with pure gold; and he covered the altar with cedar.
And Shlomo overlaid the house from within with pure gold; and he barred with chains of gold before the Sanctuary, and he overlaid it with gold.
And the whole house he overlaid with gold, until all the house was finished; and the whole altar that by the Sanctuary he overlaid with gold.
And he made within the Sanctuary two cherubim olive-wood, ten cubits its height.
And five cubits the one wing of the cherub, and five cubits the other wing of the cherub; ten cubits from the uttermost part of its wing to the uttermost part of its wing.
And ten cubits the other cherub; both the cherubim of one measure and one form.
The height of the one cherub ten cubits, and so the other cherub.

And he set the cherubim within the inner house; and they stretched forth the wings of the cherubim, and the wing of the one touched the wall, and the wing of the other cherub touched the other wall; and their wings in the midst of the house touched one another.
And he overlaid the cherubim with gold.
And all the walls of the house he surrounded with figures, carved figures of cherubim and palm trees and open flowers; from within and for the one without.
And the floor of the house he overlaid with gold; for the one within and for the one without.
And for the entrance of the Sanctuary, he made doors olive-wood; the lintel and sideposts of five parts.
And two doors of olive-wood, and he carved upon them carvings of cherubim and palm trees and open flowers, and he overlaid with gold; and spread the gold upon the cherubim, and upon the palm trees.
And he made likewise for the entrance of the temple sideposts of olive-wood, of four parts.
And two doors of cypress wood; the two leaves of the one door folding, and the two leaves of the other door folding.
And he carved cherubim and palm trees and open flowers; and he overlaid with gold fitted upon the carved work.
And he built the inner court with three rows of hewn stone and a row of cut cedar beams.
In the fourth year was the foundation of the house of Havayah laid, in the month of Ziv.
And in the eleventh year, in the month Bul, which is the eighth month, the house was finished throughout all the parts thereof, and according to all the fashion of it, and he built it seven years.
And Shlomo built his house thirteen years and he finished all his house.

And he built the house of the forest of Levanon; one hundred cubits its length, and fifty cubits its breadth, and thirty cubits its height, on four rows of cedar pillars, and cut beams of cedar upon the pillars.
And it was covered with cedar above on the walls which on forty-five pillars, fifteen each row.
And windows three rows, and window was opposite the window three times.
And all the entrances and posts square, the window; and window was opposite the window three times.
And he made the porch of pillars; fifty cubits its length, and thirty cubits its breadth, and a porch before them, and pillars and thick beams before them.
And he made a porch for the throne where he might judge, the porch of judgment; and covered with cedar from one side of the floor to the other.
And his house he might dwell, the other court, within the porch, was of the like work; and the house he would make for Paroh's daughter, whom Shlomo had taken, like this porch.
All these precious stones, according to the measures of hewn stones, sawed with saws within and without; and from the foundation up the coping, and from the outside until the great court.
And the foundation of precious stones, great stones; stones of ten cubits and stones of eight cubits.
And above precious stones, according to the measures of hewn stones and cedars.
And the great court round about three rows of hewn stones, and a row of cut beams of cedar, and for the inner court of the house of Havayah, and for the porch of the house.
And king Shlomo sent and fetched Chiram out of Tzor.

He a widow's son, of the tribe of Naftali, and his father was a man of Tzor, a coppersmith; and he was filled with the wisdom and understanding and skill, to work all works in copper; and he came to king Shlomo and wrought all his work.
And he cast the two pillars of copper, eighteen cubits the height of each pillar, and a line of twelve cubits did encompass it about, and so the other pillar.
And he made two chapiters, to set upon the tops of the pillars, molten copper; five cubits the height of the one chapiter, and five cubits the height of the other chapiter.
Nets of checker-work, wreaths of chain-work, for the chapiters which upon the top of the pillars; seven for the one chapiter, and seven for the other chapiter.
And he made the pillars; and two rows round about upon the one net-work, to cover the chapiters that upon the top, with pomegranates; and so he did for the other chapiter.
And the chapiters that upon the top of the pillars of lily work in the porch, four cubits.
And chapiters above also upon the two pillars, over against the belly which by the net-work; and the pomegranates two hundred in rows round about upon each chapiter.
And he set up the pillars in the porch of the temple; and he set up the right pillar, and called the name thereof Yachin; and he set up the left pillar, and called the name thereof Boaz.
And upon the top of the pillars lily-work; so was the work of the pillars finished.
And he made the molten sea, ten cubits from brim to brim; it round all about, and the height thereof five cubits; and a line of thirty cubits did compass it round about.
And under the brim knops compassing it round about, for ten cubits, compassing the sea round about; the knops cast in two rows, when it was cast.

It stood on twelve oxen, three looking toward the north, and three looking toward the west, and three looking toward the south, and three looking toward the east; and the sea upon them above, and all their hinder parts inward.
And it a hand-breadth thick, and the brim thereof wrought like the brim of a cup, with flowers of lilies; it contained two thousand measures.
And he made the ten bases of copper; four cubits the length of one base, and four cubits its breadth, and three cubits its height.
And the work of the bases in this; they had borders, and the borders between the ledges.
And on the borders that between the ledges lions, oxen, and cherubim; and on the ledges a base above; and beneath the lions and oxen wreaths of thin work.
And each base had four copper wheels, and tablets of copper, and the four corners thereof had undersetters; under the laver the undersetters were molten, at the side of each wreaths.

And the mouth of it within the chapiter and above a cubit, and the mouth thereof round the work of a base, a cubit and a half; and also upon its mouth gravings, and their borders foursquare, not round.
And the four wheels underneath the borders, and the axeltrees of the wheels in the base; and the height of each wheel a cubit and half a cubit.
And the work of the wheels like the work of a chariot wheel; their axeltrees, and their naves, and their felloes, and their spokes, all molten.
And four undersetters at the four corners of each base; the undersetters of the base itself.
And in the top of the base a round compass of half a cubit high; and on the top of the base its ledges and its borders of it.
And he graved on the tablets, on its ledges, and on its borders, cherubim, lions, and palm trees, according to the attachment of each, with wreaths round about.
After this he made the ten bases one casting, one measure, and one size to all of them.
And he made ten lavers of brass, each laver contained forty measures, and every laver four cubits; one laver upon each of the ten bases.
And he set the bases, five on the right side of the house, and five on the left side of the house; and he set the sea on the right side of the house eastward, toward the south.
And Chiram made the lavers, and the shovels, and the basins. And Chiram finished doing all the work which he did for king Shlomo the house of Havayah.
The two pillars, and the two bowls of the chapiters that on the top of the pillars; and the two net-works, to cover the two bowls of the chapiters which on the top of the pillars.
And the four hundred pomegranates for the two net-works, two rows of pomegranates for each net-work, to cover the two bowls of the chapiters that upon the pillars.
And the ten bases, and the ten lavers on the bases.
And the one sea, and the twelve oxen under the sea.
And the pots, and the shovels, and the basins, and all these vessels, which Chiram made for king Shlomo the house of Havayah, of bright copper.
In the plain of the Yarden did the king cast them, in the thick clay, between Sukkot and Tzareitan.
And Shlomo left all the vessels, because very very many; the weight of the copper was not found out.
And Shlomo made all the vessels of that in the house of Havayah; the altar of gold, and the table whereupon the showbread, of gold.
And the candlesticks, five on the right, and five on the left, before the Sanctuary, of pure gold; and the flowers, and the lamps, and the tongs, of gold.

And the bowls, and the musical instruments, and the basins, and the spoons, and the censors, of pure gold; and the hinges, for the doors of the inner house, the most holy, for the doors of the house, of the temple, of gold.

And all the work that king Shlomo had wrought in the house of Havayah was finished. And Shlomo brought in the things which Dovid his father had dedicated; the silver, and the gold, and the vessels, put them in the treasuries of the house of Havayah.

Then Shlomo assembled the elders of Yisroel, and all the heads of the tribes, the princes of the fathers' of the children of Yisroel, unto king Shlomo in Yerushalayim; to bring up the ark of the covenant of Havayah out of the city of Dovid, which is Tziyon.
And all the men of Yisroel assembled themselves unto king Shlomo at the feast in the month Eitanim, which the seventh month.
And all the elders of Yisroel came, and the priests took up the ark.
And they brought up the ark of Havayah, and the tabernacle of meeting, and all the holy vessels which in the tabernacle, and the priests and the Leviim did bring them up.
And King Shlomo, and all the congregation of Yisroel, that were assembled unto him, with him before the ark, sacrificing sheep and oxen, that could not be counted nor numbered for multitude.
And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of Havayah to its place, into the Sanctuary of the house, to the most holy, under the wings of the cherubim.
For the cherubim spread forth wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and the staves thereof above.
And the staves were so long that the ends of the staves were seen from the holy before the Sanctuary, and they were not seen without; and they are there unto this day.
There was nothing in the ark save the two tablets of stone which Moshe put there at Chorev, when Havayah made with the children of Yisroel, when they came out of the land of Mitzrayim.
And it came to pass, when the priests came out of the holy, and the cloud filled the house of Havayah.
And the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud; for the glory of Havayah filled the house of Havayah.
Then Shlomo said, "Havayah said that He would dwell in the thick darkness.
I have surely built You a house to dwell in; a settled place for You to dwell in forever."
And the king turned his face about, and blessed all the congregation of Yisroel, and all the congregation of Yisroel stood.
And he said, "Blessed Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel Who spoke with His mouth unto Dovid my father, and has fulfilled it with His hand, saying.

'Since the day that I brought forth My people Yisroel out of Mitzrayim, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Yisroel to build a house, that My name might be therein; but I chose Dovid to be over My people Yisroel.'
And it was in the heart of Dovid my father to build a house for the name of Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel.
And Havayah said to Dovid my father, 'Since it was in your heart to build a house unto My name, you did well that it was in your heart.
Nevertheless, you shall not build the house; but your son that shall come forth out of your loins, he shall build the house for My name.'

And Havayah has established His word that He spoke, and I have risen up in the place of Dovid my father, and sit on the throne of Yisroel, as Havayah spoke, and have built a house for the name of Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel.
And I have set there a place for the ark, wherein the covenant of Havayah, which He made with our fathers, when He brought them out of the land of Mitzrayim."
And Shlomo stood before the altar of Havayah in the presence of all the congregation of Yisroel, and spread forth his hands towards heaven.
And he said, "Havayah Elokim of Yisroel, no Elokim like you, in heaven above, or on earth beneath, Who keeps covenant and mercy with Your servants that walk before You with all their heart.
Who has kept with Your servant Dovid my father that which You spoke to him, and You spoke with Your mouth, and fulfilled it with Your hand, as this day.

And now, Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel, keep with Your servant, Dovid my father, that which You spoke to him, saying, 'There shall not fail you a man before Me to sit on the throne of Yisroel, if only your children take heed to their way, to walk before Me as you have walked before Me.'
And now, Elokim of Yisroel, please let Your word come true, which You spoke to Your servant Dovid, my father.
But will Elokim indeed dwell on the earth? Behold the heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain You; much less this temple that I have erected.
And You shall turn toward Your servant's prayer and to his supplication, O Havayah my Elokim: to hearken to the song and to the prayer that Your servant is praying before You today.
That Your eyes may be open toward this house night and day, toward the place which You said, 'My Name will be there;' to listen to the prayer that Your servant will pray toward this place.
And You shall listen to the supplication of Your servant and of Your people Yisroel that they will pray toward this place; and You shall hear in heaven, Your abode, and You shall hear and forgive.
If a man sins against his neighbor, and an oath be exacted of him to cause him to swear, and he come and swear before Your altar in this house.
And You shall hear in heaven, and do, and judge Your servants, condemning the wicked, to bring his way upon his head; and justifying the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness.
When Your people Yisroel are struck down before the enemy, because they sin against You, and shall turn again to You, and praise Your name, and pray and make supplication to You in this house.
And You shall hear in heaven, and forgive the sin of Your people Yisroel, and bring them back to the land which You gave to their fathers.
When heaven is shut up, and there is no rain, because they have sinned against You; and they shall pray toward this place and praise Your name, and repent of their sin, so that You may answer them.

And You shall hear in heaven, and forgive the sin of Your servants, and of Your people Yisroel, when You teach them the good way wherein they should walk; and give rain upon Your land, which You have given to Your people for an inheritance.

If there be famine in the land, if there be pestilence, blasting, yellowing, locust, if there be destroying locusts; if their enemy besiege them in the land of their cities, whatsoever plague, whatsoever sickness.
Any prayer, any supplication, which will be by any man, by all Your people Yisroel, who shall know every man the plague of his own heart, and spread forth his hands toward this house.
And You shall hear in heaven Your dwelling place, and forgive, and do, and give to every man according to his ways, whose heart You know, for You, alone, know the hearts of all the children of men.
That they may fear You all the days that they live in the land which You gave to our fathers.
And also to the stranger, who not of Your people Yisroel, but will come from a far country for the sake of Your Name.
For they shall hear of Your great Name, and of Your mighty hand, and of Your outstretched arm, and he will come and pray toward this house.

You shall hear in heaven Your dwelling place, and do according to all that the stranger calls You for, that all peoples of the earth may know Your Name, to fear You, as Your people Yisroel, and that they may know that Your Name is called upon this house that I have built.
If Your people go out to battle against their enemy, by what way You send them, and pray to Havayah toward the city that You have chosen, and the house that I have built for Your name.
And you shall hear in heaven their prayer and supplication, and maintain their cause.

If they sin against You, for no man who does not sin, and You will be angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, and their captors will carry them away captive to the land of the enemy, far or near.

And they shall bethink themselves in the land where they were carried captive, and repent, and make supplication to You in the land of their captors, saying, 'We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness.'

And they shall return to You with all their heart, and with all their soul, in the land of their enemies, who led them away captive, and pray to You toward their land, which You gave to their fathers, the city that You have chosen, and the house which I have built for Your Name.
And you shall hear their prayer and their supplication in heaven, Your dwelling place, and maintain their cause.
And forgive Your people what they have sinned against You, and all their transgressions that they have transgressed against You, and give mercy before their captors, that they may have mercy on them.
For they are Your people, and Your inheritance, whom You have taken out of Mitzrayim, from within the smelting furnace of iron.
That Your eyes may be open to the supplication of Your servant, and to the supplication of your people Yisroel, to hearken to them whenever they call out to You.
For You set them apart from among all the peoples of the earth, Your inheritance, as You spoke through Moshe Your servant, when You brought our fathers out of Mitzrayim, O Havayah, Elokim."
And it was, as Shlomo finished praying all this prayer and supplication to Havayah, that he arose from before the altar of Havayah, from kneeling on his knees with his hands spread out toward heaven.
And he stood, and blessed the entire congregation of Yisroel a loud voice, saying,
"Blessed Havayah, Who has given rest to His people Yisroel, according to all that He spoke; there has not failed one word of all his good word, that He spoke through Moshe His servant.
May Havayah our Elokim be with us, as He was with our forefathers; let Him not leave us, nor forsake us.
That He may incline our hearts to Him, to go in all His ways, and to keep His commandments, and His statutes, and His judgments, which He commanded our forefathers.

And may these words of mine, with which I have made supplication before Havayah, be close to Havayah our Elokim, day and night, that He sustain the cause of His servant and the cause of His people Yisroel, each day's need granted on its day.
So that all the peoples of the earth may know that Havayah is Elokim: there is none else.
Let your heart,, be whole with Havayah our Elokim, to follow His statutes and to keep His precepts as of this day.
And the King and all Yisroel with him slaughtered sacrifices before Havayah.

And Shlomo slaughtered the peace- offerings that he slaughtered to Havayah, twenty-two thousand oxen, and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep. The King and all the children of Yisroel inaugurated the Temple of Havayah.

On that day the King consecrated the middle of the court that was before the Temple of Havayah, for there he offered the burnt-offerings the meal-offerings and the fat of the peace-offerings, for the copper altar that was before Havayah was too small to contain the burnt-offerings the meal-offerings and the fat of the peace-offerings.

Now Shlomo observed the Feast at that time and all Yisroel with him, a great assemblage from the entrance of Chamat to the brook of Mitzrayim, before Havayah our Elokim, seven days and seven days, fourteen days.

On the eighth day he dismissed the people, and they blessed the King and went to their homes, rejoicing and delighted of heart for all the goodness that Havayah had wrought for Dovid His servant and for Yisroel His people.
And it was when Shlomo had finished building the Temple of Havayah and the King's palace and all Shlomo's desire that he wished to make.
Havayah appeared to Shlomo a second time as He had appeared to him in Givon.

And Havayah spoke to him: "I have heard your prayer and your petition, which you have petitioned before Me. I have consecrated this Temple which you have built to place My name there forever, and My eyes and My heart shall be there at all times.
As for You, if you go before Me, as Dovid your father went wholeheartedly and with uprightness to do in accordance with all that I have commanded you you will keep My statutes and laws.
I will establish the throne of your kingdom over Yisroel forever as I have spoken to Dovid your father, saying: A man will not fail you upon the throne of Yisroel.

But if you and your children turn away from following Me, and you will not adhere to My commandments and My statutes, which I have placed before you, but go and worship other deities and bow before them.

Then I will cut Yisroel off, from the land which I have given to them, and this house which I have made sacrosanct for My Name will I dismiss from My presence, and Yisroel shall be for a proverb and a byword among all nations.
And this Temple is exalted, and every passerby shall be astounded and will hiss, and they will say: "Why has Havayah done this to this country and to this Temple?"

They will be told, "Because they abandoned Havayah, their Elokim, Who delivered their forefathers out of the Land of Mitzrayim; and took hold of other deities and bowed to them and served them. Therefore, has Havayah brought all this retribution upon them. "
And it was at the end of twenty years during which Shlomo had built the two houses, the Temple of Havayah and the King's house.

Chiram, the king of Tzor, had supplied Shlomo with cedar wood, and with cypress wood, and with gold, as according to all his wishes, then king Shlomo gave Chiram in return twenty cities in the land of Galil.
And Chiram left Tzor to see the cities that Shlomo had given him, and they did not please him.
And he said: "What are these cities that you have given me, my brother?" And he called them the land of Kavul, which they are called this day.
And Chiram sent to the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold.
And this is the matter of the tax levy which king Shlomo raised; to build the Temple of Havayah, and his own house and the Millo, and the wall of Yerushalayim and Chatzor and Megiddo and Gezer.
Paroh, king of Mitzrayim, had gone up and conquered Gezer and burnt it with fire, and slayed the Kena'anim who inhabited the city; and he gave it as a gift to his daughter, Shlomo's wife.
And Shlomo built Gezer and the lower Beit-Choron.
And Ba'alat and Tadmor in the desert in the land.

And all the store-cities that Shlomo had and the cities of his chariots and the cities of his riders and Shlomo's desire that he desired to build in Yerushalayim and in Levanon and in all the land of his sovereignty.
All the remaining people of the Emorim, Chittim, the Perizim, the Chivim, the Yevusim, who were not of the children of Yisroel.
Their children who remained after them, in the land, whom the Children of Yisroel were unable to annihilate, of them did Shlomo raise a levy of forced labor until this day.
But of the Children of Yisroel, Shlomo made no levy of forced labor, because they were the warriors, his servants, his officers, his commanders, and the officers of his chariots and his horsemen.
These were the commanders over officers who were over Shlomo's work, five hundred and fifty, who ruled over the people who engaged in the work.
But Paroh's daughter came up from the City of Dovid to her house, which Shlomo had built for her, then he built the Millo.
And three times in a year did Shlomo offer up burnt-offerings and peace-offerings upon the altar he had built to Havayah, burning upon it incense that was before Havayah, so he completed the Temple.
King Shlomo made a ship in Etzion Gever, which is beside Eilot on the shore of the Yam Suf, in the land of Edom.
And Chiram sent in ships his servants, seafarers, those navigators of the sea, with Shlomo's servants.
And they came to Ofir, and obtained from there gold-four hundred and twenty talents, and delivered to King Shlomo.
When the Queen of Sheva heard of Shlomo's fame, because of the name of Havayah, and she came to test him with riddles.
And she came to Yerushalayim with a very large retinue, with camels bearing spices and very much gold and precious stones; and when she came to Shlomo she spoke with him all that was in her heart.
And Shlomo answered all her questions; nothing was hidden from the king that he did not tell her.
And when the Queen of Sheva had seen all Shlomo's wisdom and the house that he had built.

And the food of his table, and the seating of his servants and the station of his attendants and their attire and his cupbearers and his ascent by which he would go up to the Temple of Havayah, she was breathless.
And she said to the king; "It was a true report that I heard in my country of your deeds and of your wisdom.

However, I did not believe the words until I came and saw with my own eyes, and I have beheld that not even a half had been told to me. You have wisdom and goodness in excess of that which I have heard.
Fortunate are your men; fortunate are these your servants who always stand before you and listen to your profound wisdom.
Blessed be Havayah your Elokim, who preferred to place you on the throne of Yisroel; because of Havayah's love for Yisroel forever, He appointed you as king to do justice and righteousness.

And she gave the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold and very many spices and precious stones; there had never arrived such an abundance of spices as those which the Queen of Sheva gave to king Shlomo.
Also Chiram's ships that delivered gold from Ofir, brought from Ofir a huge quantity of almog-wood and precious stones.

And the king made of the almog-wood a path to the House of Havayah and to the king's palace, harps and psalteries to the vocalists, there had come no such almog-wood nor has there been seen to this day.
And King Shlomo gave the Queen of Sheva all her wish that she requested, aside from what he gave her, according to king Shlomo's ability; and she turned and went to her land, she and her servants.
The weight of gold which came to Shlomo in one year was 666 talents of gold.
Aside from merchants and the commerce of spice-peddlers and all the dependent kings and the regents of the land.
And king Shlomo made two hundred body shields of malleable gold; six hundred gold he would put into one body shield.
And three hundred shields of beaten gold, three manehs of gold he would put into one shield, and the king placed them in the house of the forest of Levanon.
And the king made an immense ivory throne, and overlaid it with glittering gold.
There were six steps to the throne and the top of the throne was circular from behind, and there were arms on both sides by the place of the seat, and two lions standing beside the arms.
And twelve lions stood there on the six steps on one side and on the other; no such throne was made for any kingdom.

And all of the king's drinking vessels were of gold, and all the utensils of the house of the forest of Levanon were of pure gold; none was of silver, it was reckoned with as nothing in the days of Shlomo.
For the king had at sea ships of Tarshish with Chiram's ships; once in three years, the ships of Tarshish would come bearing gold and silver, ivory and monkeys and peacocks.
Now King Shlomo transcended all the kings of the earth in affluence and wisdom.
And all the the earth sought Shlomo's presence to hear the wisdom with which Elokim had endowed him.
And each one would bring his gift, vessels of silver and vessels of gold, garments, weapons, spices, horses, and mules, the tribute due each year in its year.
Shlomo assembled chariots and horsemen, and he had a thousand and four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen; he led them in the chariot cities and with the king in Yerushalayim.
And the king made silver as common in Yerushalayim as stones, and cedars as common as sycamores, that are in the low lands in abundance.
And the source of Shlomo's horses was from Mitzrayim and an assemblage. The agents of the king, would buy the assemblage privileges for a price.

A chariot that went up and left Mitzrayim went for a price of six hundred silver, and a horse for one hundred fifty, and so for all the kings of the Chittim and for the kings of Aram did they export them through them.
King Shlomo loved many foreign women and the daughter of Paroh; Moavim, Amonim, Edomim, Tzidonim, and Chittim.

Of the nations about which Havayah had said to the Children of Yisroel, "You shall not go among them and they shall not come among you, for certainly they will sway your heart after their dieties." To these did Shlomo cleave to love.
And he had seven hundred royal wives and three hundred concubines, and his wives turned away his heart.
And it was at the time of Shlomo's old age, that his wives turned away his heart after other deities, and his heart was not whole with Havayah, His Elokim, like the heart of Dovid his father.
And Shlomo went after Ashtoret, the goddess of the Tzidonim and after Milkom the abomination of the Amonim.
And Shlomo did what was displeasing to Havayah, and he was not completely devoted to Havayah as was Dovid his father.
Then did Shlomo build a high place for Kemosh, the abomination of Moav on the mountain that is before Yerushalayim and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Amon.
And so he did for all of his alien wives who offered incense and slaughtered sacrifices to their deities.
And Havayah became angry with Shlomo because his heart had digressed from Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel, Who had appeared to him twice.
And had commanded him pertaining this matter, not to follow other deities; however, he did not keep what Havayah had commanded.

And Havayah said to Shlomo, "For as this has been with you, and you have not observed My covenant and My statutes which I have commanded you, I will surely tear the kingdom from you, and I shall give it to your servant.
However, in your days I will not do this, for the sake of Dovid your father; from the hands of your son I shall tear it.
But I shall not tear the entire kingdom away from you; one tribe I shall grant to your son for the sake of Dovid My servant, and for the sake of Yerushalayim, the city which I have chosen.
And Havayah raised up an adversary against Shlomo, Hadad, the Edomi; he was of the royal lineage in Edom.
And it was when Dovid was in Edom that Yoav, the commander of the army had gone up to bury the slain, since he had slain every male in Edom.
For Yoav and all of Yisroel remained there for six months until he had killed every male in Edom.
Adad fled, he and some Edomi men, of his father's servants with him, to go to Mitzrayim; Hadad being yet a small child.

And they set out from Midyan and came to Paran, and they took men with them from Paran and they arrived in Mitzrayim and came before Paroh, the king of Mitzrayim, He granted him a home and assigned him sustenance and gave him land.
And Hadad pleased Paroh very much so that he gave him in marriage the sister of his wife, the sister of Tachpenes, the queen.
And the sister of Tachpenes bore him Genuvat his son, whom Tachpenes weaned in Paroh's house, and Genuvat was in Paroh's house among Paroh's children.
Hadad heard in Mitzrayim that Dovid slept with his fathers and that Yoav, the commander of the army had died. And Hadad said to Paroh, "Give me leave, and I shall go to my country."
And Paroh said to him, "What do you lack with me that you desire to go to your country?" And he said, "Nevertheless, give me leave."
And Elokim raised up against him an adversary, Rezon, the son of Elyada, who had fled from Hadadezer, the king of Tzovah, his master.
And he assembled men around him, and he became commander over a battalion when Dovid slew them, and they went to Damesek and settled there and ruled in Damesek.
And he was an adversary to Yisroel all of Shlomo's days with the evil that was caused by Hadad, and he detested Yisroel and ruled over Aram.
And Yarovam the son of Nevat an Efraimi of Zeradah, whose mother's name was Zeruah, a widow; he was Shlomo's servant, he raised his hand against the king.
And this was the matter which he raised his hand against the king; Shlomo built up the Millo and closed up the breach of the city of Dovid, his father.
And the man Yarovam was a mighty man of valor; and Shlomo saw this young man, that he was a diligent worker, and he appointed him in charge of all the burdens of the House of Yosef.

And it came to be at that time when Yarovam had left Yerushalayim, that Achiyah, the Shilonit, the prophet, found him on the way, and he was wearing a new garment, and the two of them were alone in the field.
And Achiyah grasped the new garment that was upon him and tore it into twelve pieces.
And he said to Yarovam, "Take for yourself ten pieces, for so has Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel, said, "I shall tear the kingdom out of Shlomo's hands and I shall give you the ten tribes.
But he will have one tribe, for My servant Dovid's sake and for Yerushalayim's sake, the city which I have chosen of all the tribes of Yisroel.

Since they have deserted Me and have prostrated themselves to Ashtoret, the goddess of the Tzidonim, to Kemosh, Elokim of Moav, and Milkom, Elokim of the children of Amon, and they have not walked in My ways, to do what is right in My eyes to keep My statutes and judgments as did Dovid his father.

However, I will not take any part of the kingdom away from him but I will make him a king all the days of his life for the sake of Dovid My servant, whom I chose, for he kept My commandments and My statutes.
However, I will take the kingdom away from his son and will give it to you, the ten tribes.
And his son I shall give one tribe so that Dovid My servant may have a kingdom before Me in Yerushalayim, the city which I chose for Myself to place My name there.
And I shall take you, and you shall rule over all that your soul desires, and you shall be king over Yisroel.

And it will be, if you heed all that I shall command you and will walk in My ways and do what is righteous in My eyes, to keep My statutes and My commandments as did Dovid My servant, and I shall be with you and build for a lasting dynasty as I have built for Dovid My servant, and I shall give Yisroel to you.
And I shall afflict Dovid's descendants because of this, but not for all times."
Shlomo sought to put Yarovam to death, but Yarovam arose and fled to Mitzrayim to Shishak, the king of Mitzrayim, and remained in Mitzrayim until Shlomo's death.
The rest of the events of Shlomo and all that he did and his wisdom; they are assuredly written in the book of the words of Shlomo.
The years which Shlomo reigned in Yerushalayim over all Yisroel were forty years.
And Shlomo slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of Dovid his father; and Rechavam his son ruled in his place.
And Rechavam went to Shechem, for all Yisroel had gone to Shechem to make him king.
And it was when Yarovam the son of Nevat heard of this when he was yet in Mitzrayim where he had fled from the presence of king Shlomo, and Yarovam had settled in Mitzrayim.
And they sent and called him, and Yarovam and all the congregation of Yisroel came, and spoke to Rechavam saying,
"Your father made our yoke hard. Now you lighten your father's hard work and his heavy yoke which he placed upon us, and we shall serve you."
And he said to them "Go away for three days, then return again to me." And the people departed.
And king Rechavam took counsel with the elders who had attended Shlomo his father while he was yet alive saying: "What counsel do you give me to reply to this people?"

And they spoke to him saying, "If you will be a servant to this people today, and you will minister to them and you will respond to them and speak kind words to them, then they will be your servants for all times.
But He disregarded the counsel of the elders who advised him, and he took counsel with the young men who had grown up with him and who were attending him.
And he said to them: "What do you advise that we reply to this people who have spoken to me saying, 'Lighten the burden which your father has placed upon us'?"

And the young men that had grown up with him spoke to him saying: "So shall you say to this people who have spoken to you saying, 'Your father has made our yoke heavy, and you make it lighter for us,' thus shall you speak to them, My little finger is thicker than my father's loins.
And now, where my father did burden you with a heavy yoke, I shall add to your yoke; my father flogged you with whips, but I will flog you with scorpions."
Yarovam and all the people came to Rechavam on the third day, as the king had spoken, saying, "Return to me on the third day."
The king replied to the people harshly, and he disregarded the counsel of the elders which they had advised him.
And he spoke to them as the counsel of the young men saying, "My father made your yoke heavy, and I shall add to your yoke; my father flogged you with whips, and I shall flog you with scorpions."
The king did not listen to the people, for it was something brought about by Havayah, in order to fulfill His word, that Havayah had spoken through Achiyah the Shilonit to Yarovam, the son of Nevat.

And all of Yisroel saw that the king did not listen to them, and they replied to the king saying: "What share do we have in Dovid? And no heritage in Yishai's son. To your homes, O Yisroel! Now see your house, Dovid," and the Bnei Yisroel went to their homes.
the children of Yisroel who dwelt in the cities of Yehudah, Rechavam ruled over them.

And king Rechavam sent Adoram who was in charge of the tax, and all of Yisroel pelted him with stones, and he died, and king Rechavam exerted himself to get up into his chariot to flee to Yerushalayim.
So Yisroel revolted against the House of Dovid until this day.

And it came to be when all of Yisroel heard that Yarovam had returned, that they sent and called him to the assembly, and they made him king over all Yisroel; there was none that followed the House of Dovid except the tribe of Yehudah alone.

And Rechavam came to Yerushalayim, and he assembled all the House of Yehudah and the tribe of Binyamin, one hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to wage war with the House of Yisroel, to return the kingdom to Rechavam, the son of Shlomo.
And the word of Elokim was to Shemiah, the man of Elokim, saying,
"Speak to Rechavam, the son of Shlomo, King of Yehudah, and to all of the house of Yehudah and Binyamin, and the rest of the people, saying,

"Thus Havayah said: 'You shall not go up and you shall not war with your brothers, the children of Yisroel; return each man to his home for this thing has been brought about by Me.' " And they heeded the word of Havayah, and they returned to go, in accordance with the word of Havayah.
And Yarovam built Shechem in the mountain of Efraim and lived there, and he went from there and built the city of Penu'el.
Yarovam then said to himself, "Now, the kingdom may return to the House of Dovid.

When this people goes up to offer sacrifices in the Temple of Havayah, in Yerushalayim, the hearts of this people will turn to their master to Rechavam the king of Yehudah, and they shall kill me and return to Rechavam, the king of Yehudah."

The king took counsel and made two golden calves, and he said to them, saying, "It is far for you to go up to Yerushalayim; here are your deities, O Yisroel, that have brought you up from the land of Mitzrayim."
And he placed one in Beit El and the other he placed in Dan.
And this thing became a sin, and the people went before the one even until Dan.
And he made the house of high places and he made priests of some of the people who were not of the sons of Levi.

And Yarovam made a festival in the eighth month on the fifteenth day of the month like the festival which was in Yehudah, and he brought up offerings on the altar; so he did in Beit El to slaughter to the calves which he had made, and he placed in Beit El the priests of the high places which he had made.

And he brought up offerings on the altar which he has made in Beit El on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, in the month that he had fabricated from his heart, and he made a festival for the children of Yisroel, and he went up to the altar to burn the incense.
And behold a man of Elokim came from Yehudah, at the command of Havayah, to Beit El, and Yarovam was standing on the altar offering sacrifices.

And he called about the altar at the command of Havayah, and he said: "Altar, altar, so Havayah said, "Behold a son will be born to the house of Dovid, Yosiah will be his name, and upon you he will slaughter all the priests of the high places who offer sacrifices on you, and human bones will they burn upon you."
And he gave a sign on that day saying: "This is the sign that Havayah has spoken." Behold the altar shall be split and the ashes that are upon it shall be spilled."

And it was, when the king heard the words of the man of Elokim, which he proclaimed concerning the altar in Beit El, that Yarovam stretched out his hand from over the altar saying: "Seize him!" And his hand that he had stretched out against him became stiff, and he could not draw his hand back to himself.
And the altar split, and the ashes fell from the altar in accordance with the sign that the man of Elokim gave by the word of Elokim.

And the King responded and said to the man of Elokim: "Entreat now Havayah your Elokim and pray for me, that my hand be drawn back to me." And the man of Elokim entreated Havayah, and the king's hand was drawn back to him, and it was as before.
The king spoke to the Man of Elokim, "Come with me to my home and dine with me, and I shall give you a gift."
The Man of Elokim said to the king; "If you give me one half of your house, I will not come with you, and I will neither eat bread nor will I drink water in this place.
For so has he commanded me by the words of Havayah saying, 'You shall not eat bread nor drink water, neither shall you return by the road by which you have come.' "
And he went by another road and he did not return by the way through which he had entered Beit El.

And an elderly prophet was sojourning in Beit El, and his son came to him and related to him all the deed that the man of Elokim had performed that day in Beit El, and the words that he had spoken to the king; they related them to their father.
And their father spoke to them: "By which road did he go?" And his sons showed him the road by which the Man of Elokim who had come from Yehudah, had departed.
And he said to his sons: "Saddle for me a donkey," and they saddled a donkey for him, and he rode on it.
And he went after the Man of Elokim and he found him sitting under a terebrinth, and he spoke to him: "Are you the Man of Elokim who came from Yehudah?" And he replied: "I am he."
And he said to him, "Come with me to my home and eat bread."
And he said: "I cannot return with you and come with you, and I shall not eat bread or drink water in this place.
For a message to me at the command of Havayah: You shall not eat bread and you shall not drink water there. 'You shall not return to go by the road with which you arrived.' "

And he said to him, "I, too, am a prophet like you, and an angel spoke to me by the command of Havayah, saying: "Bring him back to your house, and he shall eat bread and drink water.' "-He lied to him.
And he returned with him, and he ate bread in his house and he drank water.
As they were sitting at the table and the word of Havayah came to the prophet who had brought him back.

And He called the Man of Elokim who had come from Yehudah, saying, "Thus Havayah said, "Because you have rebelled against the word of Havayah, and you did not keep the commandments that Havayah your Elokim commanded you.
And you returned and ate bread and drank water in the place concerning which He spoke to you, 'You shall not eat bread nor drink water,' your corpse shall not come to the grave of your forefathers."
And it was after he had eaten bread and after he had drunk, that he saddled the donkey for the prophet whom he had brought back.
He went and a lion found him and killed him, and his corpse was thrown in the road. The donkey was standing next to it, and the lion was standing next to the corpse.
And here men were passing, and they saw the corpse thrown in the road, and the lion standing next to the corpse; they came and spoke in the city, wherein the old prophet was residing.

And the prophet that had brought him back from the way, heard and he said, "It is a Man of Elokim who rebelled against the command of Havayah, and Havayah has given him to the lion. The lion has torn him asunder and killed him, true to the word of Havayah that He had spoken concerning him."
He spoke to his sons saying, "Saddle the donkey for me," and they saddled it.
And he went. He discovered his corpse thrown in the road with the donkey and the lion standing next to the corpse; the lion had not eaten the corpse neither had it torn the donkey asunder.
The prophet carried the corpse of the Man of Elokim, and he placed it on his donkey and brought it back, and he came to the old prophet's city, to eulogize him and bury him.
He placed the corpse in his grave and they eulogized him, "Alas my brother!"
And it was after he had buried him, that he said to his children saying, "At my death you shall bury me in the grave wherein the Man of Elokim is buried; next to his bones, place my bones."
For the thing that he called out by the word of Havayah, will come to be about the altar that is in Beit El; as about all the houses of the high places which are in the cities of Shomron.

After this thing Yarovam did not return from his evil way, but he continued and made of some of the people priests of the high places. Anyone who wished would initiate himself and become the priests of the high places.
And because of this matter, was the iniquity of the house of Yarovam; and to cut it off and destroy it from the face of the earth.
At this time Aviyah, the son of Yarovam, fell sick.

And Yarovam said to his wife, "Arise now and disguise yourself so that should not know that you are the wife of Yarovam, and you shall go to Shilo, behold there is Achiyah, the prophet; He spoke about me that be king over this people.
And you shall take in your hand ten loaves and biscuits and a flask of honey, and come to him. He will tell you what will be of the child."
And Yarovam's wife did so, and she arose and went to Shilo and came to the house of Achiyah; Achiyah could not see for his eyes were still because of his advanced age.

Now Havayah had said to Achiyah, "Behold the wife of Yarovam is coming to ask of you concerning her son as he is sick; you shall speak to her thus and thus." And it was, when she arrived she was disguised.
And it was as Achiyah heard the sound of her footsteps into the doorway, that he said, "Come in, Yarovam's wife. Why are you disguised? I am sent to you to tell you harsh tidings.
Go say to Yarovam, So has Havayah Elokim of Yisroel said, 'Since I raised you from amidst the people and I made you the ruler over my people Yisroel.

And I tore the kingdom from the House of Dovid and I gave it to you. But you have not been like My servant Dovid, who heeded My commandments and who followed Me with all his heart to do only what was proper in My eyes.
And you have done worse than all that were before you and you have gone and made for yourself foreign deities and molten images to anger Me, and you have cast Me behind your back.

Therefore, I shall bring disaster on the house of Yarovam, and I will cut off from Yarovam every male child and those who are restrained and those who are free in Yisroel, and I will expunge after the house of Yarovam as one expunges dung, until it is completed.
The dead of Yarovam in the city the dogs shall eat, and the dead in the field, the birds of the heaven shall eat, because Havayah has spoken.
And you arise and go to your house; as your feet come into the city, the child shall die.

And all of Yisroel shall eulogize him and bury him, for he alone of Yarovam shall come to a grave, because there is found in him a good deed toward Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel, in the House of Yarovam.
And Havayah shall raise for Himself a king over Yisroel who shall cut off the house of Yarovam this day, and also those who will be from now on.

And Havayah shall smite Yisroel as a reed sways in the water, and He will uproot Yisroel from this good land that He has given to your fathers and He will scatter them on the other side of the river because they have made their trees of idol worship which anger Havayah.
And he will put Yisroel because of the sins of Yarovam that he sinned and that he has caused Yisroel to sin."
And Yarovam's wife arose, and she went and arrived in Tirtzah; she came onto the threshold of the house, and the youth died.
And all of Yisroel buried him and eulogized him as the word of Havayah that He spoke through his servant Achiyah the Shilonit.
And the rest of the events of Yarovam that he fought and how he ruled are written in the book of Chronicles of the kings of Yisroel.
And the days that Yarovam reigned were twenty-two years and he slept with his forefathers, and his son Nadav ruled instead of him.

And Rechavam the son of Shlomo ruled in Yehudah; forty-one years of age was Rechavam when he became king and seventeen years he reigned in Yerushalayim, the city that Havayah had chosen to place His Name there out of all the tribes of Yisroel, and his mother's name was Na'amah the Amonit.
And Yehudah did what displeased Havayah, and they angered Him more than their forefathers had done with their sins that they sinned.
And they, too, built for themselves high places, monuments and trees for idol worship on every high hill and under every green tree.
And also adultery was in the land; they did as all the abominations of the nations that Havayah had driven out from before the Children of Yisroel.
And it came to pass in the fifth year of king Rechavam, that Shishak, the king of Mitzrayim, came up against Yerushalayim.
And he took the treasures of the House of Havayah and the treasures of the king's palace, and he took everything; and he took all the golden shields that Shlomo had made.
