King Rechavam made copper shields instead of them, and he put them under the jurisdiction of the captain of the runners that guarded the door of the king's palace.
And it was, whenever the king went to the house of Havayah, the runners would carry them and return them to the runners' chamber.
And the rest of the events of Rechavam and all that he did, they are written in the book of Chronicles of the kings of Yehudah.
And there was a war between Rechavam and Yarovam continually.
And Rechavam lay with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of Dovid, and his mother's name was Na'amah, the Amonit, and Abijam his son reigned in his place.
And in the eighteenth year of King Yarovam, the son of Nevat, Abijam ruled over Yehudah.
Three years he ruled in Yerushalayim, and his mother's name was Ma'achah the daughter of Avishalom.
And he went in all the sins of his father that he had done before him, and his heart was not complete with Havayah, his Elokim, as was the heart of Dovid his father.
For because of Dovid, Havayah his Elokim gave him rule in Yerushalayim to set up his son after him to preserve Yerushalayim.
Since Dovid did what was just in the eyes of Havayah and he did not turn away from all that Havayah had commanded him, all the days of his life, except in the matter of Uriyah the Chitti.
And there was war between Rechavam and between Yarovam all the days of his life.
And the rest of the events of Abijam and all that he did are written in the book of Chronicles of the kings of Yehudah. And there was war between Abijam and Yarovam.
And Abijam slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of Dovid, and Asa his son reigned in his stead.
And in the twentieth year of Yarovam, king of Yisroel, Asa ruled over Yehudah.
Forty-one years he ruled in Yerushalayim and his mother's name was Ma'achah the daughter of Avishalom.
And Asa did what was just in the eyes of Havayah, as had done Dovid his father.
And he abolished the adulterers from the land, and he removed the idols that his fathers had made.
And also Ma'achah his mother he removed from queen, for she had made a frightful image for an Asherah and Asa cut off her image and burnt it in Kidron Valley.
The high places he did not remove, but Asa's heart was complete with Havayah all of his days.
And he brought his father's consecrated things and his own consecrated things into the house of Havayah, silver and gold and vessels.
There was war between Asa and Basha the king of Yisroel all their days.
And Basha the king of Yisroel went up against Yehudah and built a high tower, so that nobody belonging to Asa the king of Yehudah would be able to leave or enter.

And Asa took all of the silver and gold that remained in the treasuries of the house of Havayah and the treasuries of the king's house, and he entrusted them in the hands of his servants. And King Asa sent them to Ben Haddad, the son of Tabrimon the son of Chezyon, king of Aram who resided in Damesek, saying,

"There is a treaty between me and you and between my father and your father. Behold I have sent to you a bribe of silver and gold. Go abrogate your treaty with Basha, king of Yisroel, that he depart from me.

And Ben Haddad listened to king Asa, and he sent the captains of his armies against the cities of Yisroel, and he struck Ijon and Dan and Avel-Beit Ma'achah and all Kinneret with all the land of Naftali.
And as Basha heard this, he refrained from building the high tower, and he resided in Tirtzah.

King Asa proclaimed to all Yehudah without exception and they carried the stones of the high tower, and its timber with which Ba'asha had built it, and king Asa built with it Geva of Binyamin and Mitzpah.

The remainder of the acts of Asa and all his mighty deeds and all that he accomplished and the cities which he built, they are inscribed in the book of Chronicles of the kings of Yehudah. However, during his old age, he was stricken with a foot ailment.
And Asa lay with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of Dovid his father, and Yehoshafat his son reigned in his stead.
Nadav the son of Yarovam, reigned over Yisroel during the second year of Asa, king of Yehudah, and ruled over Yisroel two years.
He did what was bad in the eyes of Havayah, and he went in the way of his father and in his sin that he had caused Yisroel to sin.

And Ba'asha the son of Achiyah, of the house of Yissachar, conspired against him, and Ba'asha struck him at Gibbeton, which belonged to the Pelishtim, when Nadav and all Yisroel were laying seige to Gibbeton.
And Basha slew him in the third year of Asa the king of Yehudah and ruled in his stead.

And it was as soon as he was king, he slew all the house of Yarovam; he did not leave over any person belonging to Yarovam, until he destroyed it, according to the word of Havayah through his servant, Achiyah the Shilonit.
For the sins of Yarovam which he had sinned and caused Yisroel to sin because of his angering which he angered Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel.
And the rest of the events of Nadav and all that he did, they are inscribed in the book of Chronicles of the kings of Yisroel.
And there was war between Asa and Ba'asha the king of Yisroel, all their lives.
During the third year of Asa, king of Yehudah, Ba'asha the son of Achiyah reigned over all of Yisroel in Tirtzah twenty-four years.
And he did what was bad in the eyes of Havayah, and he went in the way of Yarovam and in his sins that he had caused Yisroel to sin.
And the word of Havayah was to Yehu, the son of Chanani about Ba'asha saying,

"Since I have elevated you from the dust, and made you prince over My people, Yisroel, and you have gone in the way of Yarovam and you have caused My people Yisroel to sin and to anger Me with their sins.
Behold I will expunge after Ba'asha and after his house, and I will make your house as the house of Yarovam the son of Nevat.
The dead of Ba'asha in the city the dogs will eat, and the dead of Ba'asha in the field the fowl of the sky will eat.
The rest of the event of Ba'asha and what he did and his mighty deeds, are written in the book of chronicles of the kings of Yisroel.
And Ba'asha lay with his fathers, and he was buried in Tirtzah, and Elah his son reigned in his place.

Nevertheless, in the hand of Yehu, the son of Chanani the prophet, was the word of Havayah concerning Ba'asha and concerning his house and because of all the iniquity which he had done in the presence of Havayah to anger Him with the work of his hands, to be as the house of Yarovam, and because he had slain him.
In the twenty-sixth year of Asa, king of Yehudah, Elah the son of Ba'asha ruled over Yisroel in Tirtzah for two years.
And his servant Zimri, captain of half the chariots, conspired against him while he was in Tirtzah drinking himself drunk in the house of Artza who was over the household in Tirtzah.
And Zimri came and smote him and slew him in the twenty-seventh year of Asa the king of Yehudah, and he reigned in his stead.
And it was when he reigned, as he sat on his throne, that he smote the entire house of Ba'asha; he did not leave him with any males nor his kinsfolk nor his friends.
And Zimri destroyed the entire house of Ba'asha as the word of Havayah which He had spoken concerning Ba'asha through Yehu the prophet.
For all the sins of Ba'asha and the sins of Elah his son that they sinned and that they caused Yisroel to sin to anger Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel, with their false deities.
The rest of the events of Elah and all that he did are they written in the book of Chronicles of the kings of Yisroel.
During the twenty-seventh year of Asa, the king of Yehudah, Zimri reigned for seven days in Tirtzah while the people were encamped around Gibbeton, of the Pelishtim.

And the people who were encamped, heard saying, "Zimri rebelled and has also slain the king" and all of Yisroel pronounced Omri the commander-in-chief of the army, king of Yisroel on that day in the camp.
And Omri and all of Yisroel went up from Gibbeton and besieged Tirtzah.
And it was when Zimri saw that the city was captured, that he went into the inner chamber of the king's palace, and he burnt over him the king's palace with fire, and he died.
Because of his sins which he sinned, to do bad in the eyes of Havayah, to go in the way of Yarovam and in his sins which he did, to cause Yisroel to sin.
And the rest of the events of Zimri and his rebellion that he rebelled, are written in the book of Chronicles of the kings of Yisroel.
Then the people of Yisroel were divided in two. Half of the people were after Tivni the son of Ginat, to proclaim him king, and half after Omri.
And the people that followed Omri overpowered those who were after Tivni, the son of Ginat. Tivni died, and Omri reigned.
In the thirty-first year of Asa the king of Yehudah, Omri ruled over Yisroel twelve years-in Tirtzah, he ruled six years.

And he bought the mountain of Shomron from Shemer for two talents of silver; he built up the mountain and called the name of the city which he built, after the name of Shemer, Havayah of the mountain, Shomron.
And Omri did what was bad in the eyes of Havayah, and he was more wicked than all those that preceded him.
He went in all the ways of Yarovam, the son of Nevat, and in his sin, that he caused Yisroel to sin, to anger Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel with their false deities.
And the rest of the actions of Omri that he accomplished and his mighty deeds that he did, are inscribed in the book of Chronicles of the kings of Yisroel.
And Omri lay with his fathers, and he was buried in Shomron, and Achav his son ruled in his stead.
Now Achav the son of Omri ruled over Yisroel, in the thirty-eighth year of Asa, king of Yehudah, and Achav the son of Omri ruled over Yisroel in Shomron twenty-two years.
And Achav did that which was bad in the eyes of Havayah more than all before him.

And it was insignificant for him to follow the sins of Yarovam, the son of Nevat, and he took as a wife Izevel, the daughter of Etba'al, the king of the Tzidonim and he went and worshipped the Baal and prostrated himself to him.
And he erected an altar to Baal in the house of Baal which he had built in Shomron.
And Achav made the "Asherah," and Achav did more to anger Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel than all the kings of Yisroel who had preceded him.

During his days, Chi'el the Beit-Eli built Yericho; with Aviram his firstborn, he laid its foundation, and with Seguv his youngest son, he set up its gates, according to the word of Havayah that He had spoken through Yehoshua, the son of Nun.
And Eliyahu the Tishbi of the settlers of Gilad said to Achav, "As Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel, whom I serve, lives, if there will be during these years dew or rain except according to my word."
And the word of Havayah came to him saying.
"Go from here and you shall turn eastward and hide in the brook of Kereit, which is before the Yarden.
And it shall be from the brook you shall drink and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.
He went and did as the word of Havayah, and he went and resided in the Brook of Kereit which is before the Yarden.
And the ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning and bread and meat in the evening, and from the brook did he drink.
And it came to pass after a time that the brook dried up because there was no rain in the land.
And the word of Havayah came to him saying.
"Arise, go to Zarefat which belongs to Tzidon and sojourn there. Behold I have commanded a widow there to feed you."

And he rose and went to Zarefat, and he came to the entrance of the city, and behold there was a widow gathering wood. He called her and said, "Please take to me a little water in a vessel and I shall drink."
And she went to take, and he called her and said, "Take to me a morsel of bread in your hand."

And she said, "As Havayah your Elokim lives, if I have a cake, but a handful of flour and a little oil in a flask. Behold, I am gathering two pieces of wood and I will come and make this for myself and for my son, and we will eat it, and we will die."
Eliyahu said to her, "Do not fear. Come and do as you said, but first make for me a small cake from there and bring it out to me, and for you and your son make last.
For thus has spoken Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel, 'The pitcher of flour shall not end nor will the flask of oil be diminished until the day Havayah gives rain upon the land.' "
She went and did as Eliyahu had said, and she and he and her household ate days.
The pitcher of flour did not end neither did the flask of oil diminish as the word of Havayah which He had spoken through Eliyahu.
And it was after these happenings, that the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, became ill; and his illness was very serious until no soul was left within him.
And she said to Eliyahu, "What is there between me and you, man of Elokim, that you have come to me to cause my sins to be remembered and to kill my son?"
And he said to her, "Give me your son." And she took him from her bosom, and she brought him up to the upstairs chamber where he was living, and he lay him on his bed.
And he called out to Havayah and said, "O Havayah my Elokim, also on the widow with whom I am sojourning have You brought evil, to kill her son?"
And he prostrated himself on the boy three times, and he called out to Havayah and said, "O Havayah, my Elokim, restore please the soul of this child within him."
And Havayah hearkened to the voice of Eliyahu and the child's soul returned within him, and he lived.
And Eliyahu took the child and he brought him down from the upstairs chamber to the house, and he gave him to his mother. And Eliyahu said, "See, your son is alive."
And the woman said to Eliyahu, "Now I know that you are a Man of Elokim and the word of Havayah that is in your mouth, is true."
And it was many days that the word of Elokim came to Eliyahu in the third year saying, "Go, appear to Achav and I will give rain upon the surface of the earth.
And Eliyahu went to appear to Achav. Now the famine was severe in Shomron.
Achav had called Ovadyah, who was over the household, and Ovadyah feared of Havayah greatly.
And it was when Izevel cut off of the prophets of Havayah, that Ovadyah took one hundred prophets and hid them fifty men in a cave, and he nourished them with bread and water.
And Achav said to Ovadyah, "Go in the land to all the wells of water and to all the brooks, maybe we will find grass, and we will save the lives of horse and mule and we will not lose all our beasts.
They divided the land between them to pass through it; Achav went on one way by himself and Ovadyah went on one way by himself.
Now Ovadyah was on the road and behold Eliyahu was in front of him. He recognized him and fell on his face, and he said, "Is this you, my master, Eliyahu? "
And he said to him, "This is I Go and tell your master 'Here is Eliyahu.' "
And he said, "What have I sinned that you have delivered your servant into the hands of Achav to kill me?

As Havayah your Elokim lives, if there is a nation or a kingdom where my master has not sent to search for you, and they have said, 'He is not there,' and he adjured the kingdom and nation that they did not find you.
And now you say, 'Go tell your master, Here is Eliyahu.'

And it will be that I will go from here, and a wind from Havayah will carry you to I know not where, and I will come to tell Achav, and he will not find you and he will kill me; yet your servant fears Havayah from my youth.
My master was surely told what I did when Izevel killed all the prophets of Havayah. I hid one hundred men of the prophets of Havayah by fifty men in a cave, and provided them with bread and water.
And now you say 'Go tell your master, "Here is Eliyahu" '; and he will kill me."
And Eliyahu said, "As Havayah of Hosts before whom I have stood, lives, I will appear to him today."
And Ovadyah went towards Achav and he told him, and Achav went towards Eliyahu.
And it was when Achav saw Eliyahu, that Achav said to him, "Is this you, the one who brings trouble upon Yisroel?"
And he said, "I have not brought trouble upon Yisroel, but you and your father's house, since you have forsaken the commandments of Havayah, and you went after the Be'alim.
And now, send and gather for me all of Yisroel to Mount Karmel, and the prophets of the Baal four hundred and fifty and the prophets of the Ashera four hundred who eat at Izevel's table.
And Achav sent among all of the Children of Yisroel, and he gathered the prophets to Mount Karmel.

And Eliyahu drew near to all the people and said, "Until when are you hopping between two ideas? If Havayah is Elokim, go after Him, and if the Baal, go after him." And the people did not answer him a word.
And Eliyahu spoke to the people, "I have remained a prophet to Havayah by myself, and the prophets of the Baal are four hundred and fifty men.

And let them give us two bulls and let them choose one bull for themselves and cut it up and place it on the wood, but fire they shall not put, and I will prepare one bull, and I will put it on the wood, and fire will I not place.

And you will call in the name of your deity, and I will call in the name of Havayah, and it will be Elokim that will answer with fire, he is Elokim." And all of the people answered and said, "The thing is good."
And Eliyahu said to the prophets of the Baal, "Choose for yourselves the one bull and prepare it first since you are the majority, and call in the name of your deity, and fire place not."

They took the bull that he gave them and prepared. And they called in the name of the Baal from the morning until noon, saying, "O Baal, answer us!" But there was no voice and no answer, and they hopped on the altar that they had made.

And it was at noon that Eliyahu scoffed at them, and he said, "Call with a loud voice, for he is a deity. He is talking or he is pursuing or he is on a journey; perhaps he is sleeping and will awaken.
And they called with a loud voice and gashed themselves as was their custom, with swords and lances, until blood gushed on them.
And as the afternoon passed and they feigned to prophesy until the time of the sacrifice of the offering, and there was no voice and no answer and no one was listening.
And Eliyahu said to all the people, "Come near to me," and all the people came near to him and he repaired the torn down altar of Havayah.
Eliyahu took twelve stones, corresponding to the number of the tribes of the sons of Yackov, to whom the word of Havayah came, saying, "Yisroel shall be your name."
He built the stones into an altar in the name of Havayah and he made a trench as great as would contain two se'ah of seed, around the altar.
And he arranged the wood, and he cut up the bull and placed upon the wood.

And he said, "Fill me four pitchers of water and pour them on the burnt-offerings and on the wood." And he said, "Repeat it," and they repeated it. And he said, "Do it a third time," and they did it a third time.
And the water went around the altar, and also the trench he filled with water.

And it was when the evening sacrifice was offered that Eliyahu the prophet came near and said, "Havayah, Elokim of Avraham, Yitzchak and Yisroel, today let it be known that You are Elokim in Yisroel and that I am Your servant, and at Your word have I done all these things.
Answer me, O Havayah, answer me, and this people shall know that You are Havayah Elokim, and You have turned their hearts backwards."
And the fire of Havayah fell and consumed the burnt offerings and the wood and the stones and the earth, and the water which was in the trench it licked up.
And all the people saw and fell on their faces, and they said, "Havayah is Elokim, Havayah is Elokim."
Eliyahu said to them, "Seize the prophets of the Baal; let no one of them escape." And they seized them. Eliyahu took them down the brook Kishon and slew them there.
And Eliyahu said to Achav, "Go up, eat and drink, for now you will hear the rumbling sound of the rain.
And Achav went up to eat and drink. Eliyahu went up to the top of Mt. Karmel and crouched on the ground, and he put his head between his knees.
And he said to his servant, "Please go up and look toward the sea." And he went up and looked, and he said, "There is nothing." And he said, "Go again" seven times.
And it was on the seventh time, that he said, "There is a cloud as small as a man's palm, rising from the sea." And he said, "Go up, say to Achav, "Hitch up and descend, lest the rain stop you."
Meanwhile, the heavens grew dark with clouds and wind, and there was a heavy rain; and Achav rode and went to Yizre'el.
And a spirit of strength from Havayah was with Eliyahu, and he girded his loins and ran before Achav until coming to Yizre'el.
And Achav told Izevel all that Eliyahu had done, and all that he had killed all of the prophets with the sword.
Izevel sent a messenger to Eliyahu saying, "So may the deities do and so may they continue unless at this time tomorrow, I will make your life like the life of one of them.
And he saw, and he arose and went for his life, and he came to Be'er Sheva which belonged to Yehudah. And he left his servant there.

He went to the desert, a distance of one day's travel, and he came and sat under a juniper and requested that his soul die, he said, "Enough, now Havayah take my soul as I am not better than my forefathers."
He lay and slept underneath one juniper, and behold! An angel touched him and said to him: "rise and eat."
And he looked, and at his head there was a cake baked on hot coals, and a flask of water. He ate and drank and again he lay down.
And the angel of Havayah returned to him again and touched him and said, "Arise and eat as the journey is too much for you."
And he arose and ate and drank, and he went with the strength of this meal forty days and forty nights up to the mountain of Havayah, Chorev.
And he came there to the cave, and he lodged there. And behold! The word of Havayah came to him. And He said to him: "What are you doing here, Eliyahu?"

And he said: "I have been zealous for Havayah, Elokim of Hosts, for the children of Yisroel have forsaken Your covenant. They have torn down Your altars and they have killed Your prophets by the sword, and I have remained alone, and they seek my life to take it.

And He said: "Go out and stand in the mountain before Havayah, behold! Havayah passes, and a great and strong wind splitting mountains and shattering boulders before Havayah, but Havayah was not in the wind. And after the wind an earthquake-not in the earthquake was Havayah.
After the earthquake fire, not in the fire was Havayah, and after the fire a still small sound.
And as Eliyahu heard, he wrapped his face in his mantle, and he went out and stood at the entrance to the cave, and behold a voice came to him and said: "What are you doing here, Eliyahu?"

And he said, "I have been zealous for Havayah, Elokim of Hosts, for the Children of Yisroel have forsaken Your covenant, they have torn down Your altars, and they have killed Your prophets by the sword, and I alone remain, and they seek my soul to take it."
And Havayah said to him: "Go, return to your way to the desert of Damesek and you shall come and anoint Chaza'el to be king over Aram.
And Yehu, the son of Nimshi, you shall anoint as king over Yisroel, and Elisha, the son of Shafat from Hevel Meholah you shall anoint to be prophet in your stead."
And it will be, those who escape the sword of Chaza'el, Yehu will kill, and those who escape the sword of Yehu, Elisha will kill.
And I will leave over in Yisroel seven thousand, all the knees that did not kneel to the Baal and every mouth that did not kiss him."
And he went from there, and he found Elisha, the son of Shafat, as he was plowing; twelve yoke were before him and he was with the twelfth, and Eliyahu went over to him and threw his mantle over him.
And he left the oxen and ran after Eliyahu and said: "Let me, please, kiss my father and my mother, and I will go after you," and he said to him, "Go, return, for what have I done to you?"

And he returned from after him, and he took the yoke of oxen and slaughtered them, and with the gear of the oxen he cooked the meat for them, and he gave the people and they ate, and he rose and followed Eliyahu and ministered to him.
And Ben-Hadad the king of Aram gathered all his army and thirty-two kings with him and horses and chariots, and he went up and besieged Shomron and waged war with it.
And he sent messengers to Achav the king of Yisroel to the city.
And he said to him: "Thus Ben-Hadad said 'Your silver and gold are mine; your beautiful wives and children are mine.' "
And the king of Yisroel answered him and said: "As you say, my master, the king, I am yours as well as all that is mine."
And the messengers returned and said, "Thus Ben said- Haddad, 'As I have sent to you saying, "Your silver and your gold, your wives, and your children you shall give to me."
But at this time tomorrow I will send my servants to you, and they will search your house and the houses of your servants, and anything you prize they will put in their hands and take it away."

And the king of Yisroel summoned all the elders of the land and said, "Please realize and see that this is looking to cause harm, for he has sent to me for my wives, my sons, and my silver and gold, and I have not denied him."
And all of the elders and all of the people said to him, "Do not obey and do not consent."

And he said to the messengers of Ben-Hadad, "Tell to your master the king, 'All that you have sent to your servant at first, I will do, but this matter I cannot do.' " And the messengers went, and they brought back the message to him.
And Ben-Hadad sent to him and said, "So shall the deities do to me and so shall they continue if the earth of Shomron suffice for the footsteps of all the people who are with me."
And the king of Yisroel answered and said: "Say, 'One who girds shall not boast as one who ungirds.' "
And it was as he heard these words as he was drinking he and the kings who were with him in pavilions, that he said to his servants, "Lay on!" and they laid siege to the city.

And behold a certain prophet approached Achav, the king of Yisroel, and said, "So Havayah said, 'Have you seen all this great multitude? Behold! I am giving them into your hands today, and you will know that I am Havayah.' "
And Achav said, "With whom?" And he said, "Thus Havayah said, 'With the youths of the governors of the provinces.' " And he said: "Who will commandeer the battle?" And he said, "You."
And he counted the youths of the governors of the provinces, and they were two hundred thirty-two, and afterwards he counted all the people, all the children of Yisroel, seven thousand.
And they went out at noon and Ben-Hadad was drinking himself drunk in the pavilions, he and the kings-the thirty-two kings who aided him.
And the youths of the governors of the provinces went out first, and Ben-Hadad sent out, and they told him saying, "Men have come out of Shomron."
And he said, "If for peace they have come out, seize them alive; If for war they have come out, alive shall you seize them."
And it was these who had come out of the city, the youths of the governors of the provinces, and the army which was after them.
And they killed every man his opponent, the Aramim fled and Yisroel chased them. And Ben-Hadad, the king of Aram escaped on horseback with horsemen.
And the king of Yisroel went out and struck the horses and the chariots and inflicted upon Aram a great defeat.
And the prophet approached the king of Yisroel and said to him, "Go, strengthen yourself and know and see what you shall do, for at the return of the year the king of Aram will come up against you."
And the servants of the king of Aram said to him: "A Elokim of mountains is their Elokim: therefore they overpowered us. However, if we fight them in the plains, if we will not overpower them.
And do this thing: Remove the kings, each man from his place, and place officers in their place.

And you shall number for yourself an army like the army that fell from you, and horse for horse and chariot for chariot, and we will fight against them in the plains, if we will not overpower them." And he heeded them and did so.
And it was at the return of the year, that Ben-Hadad counted the Aramim, and he went up to Afek to war with the children of Yisroel.
And the children of Yisroel were counted and provisioned, and they went to meet them, and the children of Yisroel encamped against them like two flocks of goats, whereas the Aramim filled the land.

And the Man of Elokim approached and said to the king of Yisroel. And he said, "Thus Havayah said, 'Because the Aramim said that Elokim of the mountains is Havayah and He is not Elokim over the valleys, I will deliver all this great multitude into your hand and you will know that I am Havayah. ' "
And they were encamped opposite each other seven days; and it was on the seventh day that battle drew closer and the children of Yisroel killed of Aram, one hundred thousand footmen in one day.
And the survivors fled to Afek, to the city, and the wall fell on the twenty-seven thousand men who had survived; Ben-Hadad fled and came into the city into a chamber within a chamber.

And his servants said to him, "Behold; we have now heard that the kings of the House of Yisroel are kindly kings. Let us put sackcloth on our loins and ropes on our heads and let us go out to the king of Yisroel, perhaps he will spare your life."

So they girded sackcloth on their loins and ropes on their heads, and they came to the king of Yisroel and said, "Your servant Ben-Hadad said, "Please, may my life be spared." And he said, "Is he still alive? He is my brother."

And the people took it for an omen, and they hastened and caught it from him and said, "Your brother Ben-Hadad." And he said, "Come and take him." Ben-Hadad went out to him, and he helped him climb up into the chariot.

And he said to him, "The cities which my father took from your father I will return, and you shall make streets for yourself in Damesek as my father had made in Shomron. And I will," "release him with this treaty." And he forged with him a treaty, and he released him.
And a certain man of the disciples of the prophets said to his friend, "By the word of Havayah, strike me now." And the man refused to hit him.
And he said to him, "because you have not obeyed Havayah, who you depart from me, a lion will strike you." And he went away from him, and a lion found him and struck him.
And he found another man and he said, "Strike me, please." And the man struck him, striking and wounding him.
And the prophet went and waited for the king on the way, and he disguised himself with his headband over his eyes.

And it was when the king was passing, that he cried out to the king, and he said, "Your servant went out in the thick of the battle, and behold a man turned aside, and he brought to me a man and said, "Watch this man for me; if he will be missing, your life will be instead of his life, or else you shall weigh out a talent of silver."
And your servant was busy here and there, and he was gone." And the king of Yisroel said to him, "So is your verdict; you have pronounced."
And he hastened and removed the headband from his eyes, and the king of Yisroel recognized him, that he was one of the prophets.

And he said to him, "Thus Havayah said, 'Because you have released the man whom I designated for destruction, from your hand, it will be your life instead of his life and your people instead of his people.' "
And the king of Yisroel went to his home sad and upset, and he came to Shomron.
And it was after these happenings, that Navot the Yizre'eli had a vineyard, which was in Yizre'el, next to the palace of Achav, the king of Shomron.

And Achav spoke to Navot saying, "Give me your vineyard and I will have it for a vegetable garden since it is near my house, and I will give you instead of it a vineyard which is better than it-if it pleases you, I will give you money, its worth."
And Navot said to Achav, "Havayah forbid me to give the inheritance of my forefathers to you."

And Achav came to his house sad and upset because of the matter that Navot the Yizre'eli had spoken to him and said, "I will not give you the inheritance of my forefathers." He lay on his bed, turned away his face, and did not eat bread.
And Izevel his wife came to him, and spoke to him, "For what is this that your spirit has left you and you do not eat bread?"

He spoke to her, "For I have spoken to Navot the Yizre'eli and I have said to him, 'Give me your vineyard for money or if you wish I will give you a vineyard instead of it. And he said, 'I will not give you my vineyard.' "
And Izevel his wife said to him, "Do you now exercise kingly power over Yisroel? Arise, and eat bread and let your heart be merry, I will give you Navot the Yizre'eli's vineyard."
And she wrote letters in Achav's name and sealed with his seal, and she sent the letters to the elders and the officials who were in his city, who sat with Navot.
And she wrote letters saying, "Proclaim a fast and place Navot in the forefront of the people.
And set up two wicked men opposite him and they will testify against him saying, 'You have cursed Elokim and the king,' and they shall remove him and stone him, and he will die."
And the men of his city did, the elders and the officials that dwelled in his city, as Izevel sent to them, as it was written in the letters that she had sent to them.
They proclaimed a fast, and they set Navot at the head of the people.

And the two wicked men came and sat opposite him, and the wicked men testified against Navot in front of the people saying, "Navot cursed Elokim and the king." And they took him out of the city and stoned him with stones, and he died.
And they sent to Izevel saying: "Navot has been stoned and has died."

And it was when Izevel heard that Navot was stoned and that he died, that Izevel said to Achav, "Get up, and take possession of the vineyard of Navot the Yizre'eli, which he refused to give you for money, for Navot is not living but dead."
And it was as Achav heard that Navot had died, that Achav got up to go down to the vineyard of Navot the Yizre'eli to take possession of it.
And the word of Havayah came to Eliyahu the Tishbi saying,
"Arise and go down toward Achav the king of Yisroel, who is in Shomron. Behold! he is in Navot's vineyard where he has gone down to take possession of it.

And you shall speak to him saying, 'So Havayah said, "Have you murdered and also inherited?" And you shall speak to him saying, 'Thus Havayah said; "In the place that the dogs have licked the blood of Navot, shall the dogs lick your blood, even yours!"'
And Achav said to Eliyahu, "Have you found me, my enemy?" And he said, "I have found because you have sold yourself to do what is bad in the eyes of Havayah.
I will bring disaster upon you and I will expunge after you and I will cut off from Achav every male child and those that are restrained and those that are free in Yisroel.
And I will make your house as the house of Yarovam, the son of Nevat and the house of Ba'asha the son of Achiyah, because of the anger which you have angered and you have caused Yisroel to sin.
And also concerning Izevel, Havayah spoke saying, 'The dogs will eat Izevel in the valley of Yizre'el.
The dead of Achav in the city will be eaten by the dogs, and the dead in the fields the fowl of the sky will eat.' "
But there was none like Achav who had sold himself to do bad in the eyes of Havayah, that Izevel his wife instigated him.
And he very abominably went after idols, like all that the Emorim had done, whom Havayah had expelled from before the children of Yisroel.
And it was when Achav heard these words, that he tore his garments and put sackcloth on his flesh and he fasted, and he lay in the sackcloth and walked slowly.
And it was the word of Havayah to Eliyahu the Tishbi saying:
"Have you seen that Achav is submissive to me? Because he has humbled himself before Me, I will not bring the disaster in his days; in the days of his son I will bring the disaster on his house."
And they lived three years; there were no wars between Aram; and Yisroel.
And it was during the third year, that Yehoshafat, the king of Yehudah came down to the king of Yisroel.
And the king of Yisroel said to his servants: "Do you know that Ramot-Gilad is ours, and we are doing nothing about taking it out of the hands of the king of Aram."
And he said to Yehoshafat, "Will you go with me to do battle in Ramot Gilad?" And Yehoshafat said to the king of Yisroel: "I am as you are, my people is as your people, my horses are as your horses."
And Yehoshafat said to the king of Yisroel: "Please inquire today the word of Havayah. "

And the king of Yisroel gathered the prophets, about four hundred men and said to them, "Shall I go on to Ramot Gilad, to do battle, or shall I refrain?" And they said, "Ascend, and Havayah will deliver into the hands of the king."
And Yehoshafat said, "Is there no other prophet of Havayah here from whom we may inquire?"

And the king of Yisroel said to Yehoshafat, "There is one more man from whom to inquire the word of Havayah, but I hate him for he does not prophesy good about me, only bad; Michayahu the son of Yimlah." And Yehoshafat said, "The king should not say so."
And the king of Yisroel summoned one eunuch, and said, "Bring Michayahu the son of Yimlah at once."

Now the king of Yisroel and Yehoshafat, king of Yehudah were seated each on his throne, dressed in attire in a threshing-floor at the entrance of the gate of Shomron, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
And Tzidkiyah the son of Kena'anah made himself iron horns, and he said, "So Havayah said, 'With these shall you gore the Aramim until you destroy them completely.' "
And all the prophets were prophesying so, saying, "Go up to Ramot-Gilad and triumph, and Havayah will deliver into the king's hand."

Now the messenger who had gone to summon Michayahu, spoke to him saying, "Behold, the words of the prophets are unanimously favorable to the king. Please let your word be like the word of one of them, and you shall speak favorably."
And Michayahu said, "As Havayah lives, for what Havayah will say to me, that will I speak."

And he came to the king, and the king said to him, "Michayahu, shall we go to Ramot-Gilad to war or shall we refrain?" And he said to him, "Go up and triumph, and may Havayah deliver it into the king's hand."
And the king said to him, "How many times must I adjure you that you shall not speak to me but truth in the name of Havayah?"
And he said, "I saw all the Bnei Yisroel scattered over the mountains like sheep who have no shepherd. And Havayah said, 'These have no master. Let them return each one to his house in peace.' "
And the king of Yisroel said to Yehoshafat, "Did I not say to you that he does not prophesy good concerning me, only bad?"
And he said, "Therefore, listen to the word of Havayah. I saw Havayah seated on His throne, and all the host of heaven were standing by Him on His right and on His left.
And Havayah said, 'Who will entice Achav so that he will go up and fall in Ramot-Gilad?' One said in this manner and another one said in that manner.
And a certain spirit came forth and stood before Havayah and said, 'I will entice him,' and Havayah said to him 'How?'
And he said, 'I will go forth, and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' And He said, 'You will entice and you will prevail. Go forth and do so.'
And now, behold Havayah has placed a lying spirit in the mouth of all these prophets of yours, whereas Havayah spoke evil concerning you."
And Tzidkiyah the son of Kena'anah approached and struck Michayahu on the cheek, and he said, "Which did the spirit of Havayah pass from me to speak with you?"
And Michayahu said, "Behold you will see on that day that you will come into a chamber within a chamber to hide."
And the king of Yisroel said, "Take Michayahu and return him to Amon the mayor of the city and to Yo'ash the king's son.
And you shall say, 'So said the king, "Place this one in prison, and feed him a scant amount of bread and a scant amount of water until I come back in peace.' "
And Michayahu said: "If you will return in peace, Havayah did not speak to me." And he said, "All the nations listen."
The king of Yisroel and Yehoshafat the king of Yehudah went up to Ramot-Gilad.
And the king of Yisroel said to Yehoshafat, " disguise and go into battle, and you wear your garb; the king of Yisroel disguised himself and went into battle.
The king of Aram commanded the thirty-two officers of his chariots saying, "Attack neither small nor great, except the king of Yisroel only."
And it was when the officers of the chariots saw Yehoshafat that they said: "This is but the king of Yisroel." They turned upon him to attack and Yehoshafat cried out.
And it was when the officers of the chariots saw that he was not the king of Yisroel, that they turned back from after him.
A man drew his bow innocently and hit the king of Yisroel between the scales and the coat of mail, and he said to his charioteer, "Turn your hand and carry me out of the camp for I have become sick."
The battle became more intense that day and the king was standing in the chariot against the Aramim. He died at evening and the blood of his wounds ran out into the inside of the chariot.
A cry passed through the camp as the sun went down saying, "Everyone to his city, every person to his country."
And the king died and was brought to Shomron, and they buried the king in Shomron.
And he washed the chariot at the pool of Shomron, and the dogs licked his blood, and they washed the weapons there as according to the word of Havayah which He had spoken.
The remainder of the deeds of Achav and all that he accomplished and the ivory palace which he built and all the cities that he built are written in the book of Chronicles of the kings of Yisroel.
Achav lay with his forefathers, and Achazyah his son reigned in his place.
Yehoshafat the son of Asa reigned over Yehudah in the fourth year of Achav the king of Yisroel.
Yehoshafat was thirty-five years of age when he became king; he reigned twenty- five years in Yerushalayim, and his mother's name was Azuvah, the daughter of Shilhi.
He went in all the ways of his father Asa-he did not veer from those ways-doing what was proper in the eyes of Havayah.
However, the high places he did not remove. The people were still sacrificing and offering in the high places.
Yehoshafat made peace with the king of Yisroel.
The rest of the acts of Yehoshafat and his heroic deeds that he performed and he fought, are written in the Chronicles of the kings of Yehudah.
The remainder of the prostitutes that remained from the days of Asa his father he purged from the land.
There was no king in Edom; a governor was king.
Yehoshafat made ships of Tarshish to go to Ofir for gold; but he did not go, since the ships were broken at Ezion-Gever.
Then Achazyah the son of Achav said to Yehoshafat, "Let my servants go with your servants in the ships," but Yehoshafat did not want.
Yehoshafat lay with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of Dovid his father, and Yehoram his son reigned in his stead.
Achazyah the son of Achav reigned over Yisroel in Shomron in the seventeenth year of Yehoshafat, king of Yehudah, and he ruled over Yisroel for two years.
He did what was bad in the eyes of Havayah. He went in the path of his father and the path of his mother, and in the path of Yarovam the son of Nevat, who had caused Yisroel to sin.
He worshipped the Baal, he bowed to him and he provoked Havayah, Elokim of Yisroel to anger, like all that his father had done.
